data.name: Devavrat
data.gender_notes: Devavrat is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devavrat is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Deva’ meaning god and ‘Vrat’ meaning bound or pledged. This name signifies a person who is deeply devoted to the divine and is bound by the vows and promises made to the gods. The name Devavrat carries the meaning “God-bound” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devavrat usually hope their child will grow to embody god-bound and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Devavrat belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God-bound.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devavrat total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Devavrat is rooted in Hindu culture and tradition. In Hinduism, devotion towards gods and goddesses is considered a noble virtue. The name brings to mind the concept of 'Bhakti' or devotion, a core aspect of Hindu spirituality. For someone bearing the name Devavrat, there is an inherent expectation to be a pious and devoted individual in society.
data.spiritual_significance: Devavrat is a symbol of religious dedication and commitment. It signifies one's strong bond with the divine and the promise to uphold that bond through vows and practices. The name Devavrat serves as a reminder of the spiritual aspirations that a person holds and their commitment to God, which can guide their actions and decisions throughout their life. It also signifies the belief that the divine grace can help one overcome both worldly and spiritual challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Deva means god, Vrat means vow or commitment. The name Devavrat symbolizes a divine being who is committed to upholding and fulfilling the duties and responsibilities of a god towards his creation. It signifies a deep sense of devotion and dedication towards the divine path.

historical_references.reference: Devavrat was a legendary king of the Haihayas, a dynasty of ancient India, who ruled in the 12th century BC in the region of Mathura in North India. He is most famous for his patronage of the arts and his extraordinary charitable deeds. His name is mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Devavrat comes from the Jaiminiya Brahmana, a text of the Yajurveda. In this text, Devavrat is mentioned as performing the Agnicayana sacrifice, which was considered a crucial rite for ensuring the fertility of the land and the prosperity of the kingdom. This reference dates back to around 1000 BCE.
